thread.title: Exxon Footage Findings

content.text: Continue tracing K1966 / AGBH009 and lab 011001250 JD: find original or authenticated footage, recorder-clock analysis, comparison photographs, examiner notes, final identification/exclusion and chain-of-custody records. Follow the five sets of 13 prints and six CD-R image products without assuming any disc contains full video. Test whether the separate October 17 possible-match memo can be matched to this specimen; do not equate them solely by Exxon description. Give independent time anchors and competing interpretations. Do not contact custodians.

Yes. The new research supports **more targeted prompts**, especially for identifying the actual Zim mover and tracing the FBI’s unfinished headquarters inquiry. I’d run the first two before the others.

**4. Can the Exxon footage establish a vehicle and time?**
```sql
Find the original or an authenticated copy of the September 11, 2001 Exxon
surveillance tape K1966/AGBH009 and all records resolving whether either
white van was associated with Urban Moving Systems.

Trace the September 28 lab request and October 18 examination under
011001250 HC JD, including submitted prints K1967–K1978, output images,
CD-Rs, examiner notes, chain of custody, comparison photographs and final
identification or exclusion. Search 011001250 JD and the draft variant
011001250 HC ID as additional locators.

Find the recorder’s clock settings, calibration, time-zone and daylight-
saving settings, independent time anchors and any clock-correction
analysis. The displayed 8:29–8:31 time is not automatically verified.

Compare the footage with vehicle records and witness accounts, including
evidence that the vehicle was different or the clock inaccurate. Report
what can and cannot be determined about occupants, location and timing.
A match alone would not prove advance knowledge. Cite original documents
and distinguish the Exxon footage from other surveillance recordings.
```

There is also a narrower prompt worth running on the **Bayoumi–Awlaki video date**: reconcile the 2024 filing’s January 1998 date with the 2022 expert report’s January 1999 date, establish whether the cited file identifiers refer to the same clip, and obtain the complete deposition context. That can test the video chronology, although it is less direct for the UMS question.
